svg.title: VulnXploit request map
svg.desc: A browser built with vanilla JavaScript and Bootstrap holds all state and calls four independent, stateless Flask routes: a scan route that runs nmap on twelve fixed ports and looks the service name up in a hard-coded three-row table, a PoC route that returns static template text with placeholders filled in, and two export routes that build a PDF and CSV from results the browser posts back; a ledger lists what the code does not do, including validation, exploitation, verification and storage.
svg.text: is run and no finding is
WHAT THE CODE DOES NOT DO · FOUND BY READING THE SOURCE
No validation, authorisation or scope control. /api/scan accepts any target
string and scans it. No private-range block, no auth, no rate limit; debug=True.
No real CVE lookup. Matching is a hard-coded 3-row dict keyed by nmap’s
service name. The version field is read but never used in the match.
No exploitation or verification. The PoC route returns static template text
with placeholders filled in; nothing is executed and no result is confirmed.
No storage, history or tests. package-lock.json lists React + axios, but the
UI is vanilla JS + Bootstrap and there is no Node server; node_modules is unused.
